input: height is a plain list of nonnegative integers, excluding bool, describing vertical lines at consecutive integer positions. Let n be its length and H its maximum height, or zero for empty input. The shared domain requires 0 <= n <= 4294967295, 0 <= H <= 9007199254740991, and mathematical max(n - 1, 0) * H <= 9007199254740991. Lengths zero and one are explicitly supported authored extensions, not a claim that the frozen problem admits them. Inputs must fit both runtimes; concurrent mutation is excluded. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: A nonnegative int equal to max((right - left) * min(height[left], height[right])) over all 0 <= left < right < n, or zero when n < 2. This is area between two selected lines, not contiguous histogram area. All-zero heights return zero.
mutation_aliasing: The caller's height list, its length and its elements remain unchanged. A scalar is returned; no input copy or persistent Solution instance state is created.
numeric: The shared bounds are n <= 4294967295, H <= 9007199254740991 and max(n - 1, 0) * H <= 9007199254740991. All arithmetic intermediates are safe integers: initial right is in [-1, n - 1], pointer updates remain in [0, n - 1] whenever the loop runs, positive widths are at most n - 1, and each computed area is at most (n - 1) * H. Minimum/maximum and comparisons select or compare bounded operands without subtraction. Python integer arithmetic is exact; the same mathematical bounds guarantee exact JavaScript Number operations. These are mathematical preconditions, not floating-point validation checks.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space under constant-cost bounded-word arithmetic and indexing. Every loop removes one endpoint, so at most max(n - 1, 0) iterations occur. Before each iteration, any pair with area greater than best has both endpoints in [left, right]. After the current pair is charged to best, a narrower pair using its shorter endpoint cannot improve best, so that endpoint can be discarded; ties discard the left endpoint.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 555 UTF-8 bytes, including comments, Solution wrapper, method and terminal newline. Every byte is charged. There are no external helpers, imports, generated source or hidden expansion. Any eventual judge adapter is additional charged source.
evidence_boundary: Independently authored dev_fit candidate outside frozen source sets. No candidate execution, predecessor equivalence, behavioral qualification, benchmark acceptance or M1 progress is claimed. The mandatory isolated judge is unavailable; static checks do not establish runtime correctness. Independent source-bound qualification must cover zero/one/two-line inputs, all-zero heights, repeated/equal endpoints, monotone and interior-optimum shapes, exact area limits and input preservation before promotion.
